title: Tongva Park at a human scale
paragraphs: I’m excited to have Tongva Park online, with seven viewpoints—the most available for any single project in LENS so far.

I enjoyed this park a lot, not only for its “heroic” formal moves, but also for the richness of its spatial layers. The shaded play slope, picnic grove and smaller seating spaces have a particularly comfortable human scale. Careful planting gives these places much of their character. For me, this is where the park’s placemaking is especially successful.
imageAlt: Curving seating, planted slopes and shaded spaces at Tongva Park in Santa Monica.

title: Architecture and public domain
paragraphs: The Broad is now on LENS, the first project in the archive to include architecture and interior spaces. What interests me here is the museum as an extension of the city’s public domain. The plaza, the sheltered edge of the building and the spaces inside belong to a connected public experience, even as their forms and materials change.

Their spatial forms, materials, design approaches and scales offer useful references for design teaching and research. I’m glad to bring them into the collection. Moving beyond this disciplinary boundary allows LENS to focus more clearly on its core mission of documenting the urban public domain and the spatial experience.
imageAlt: Illustration of The Broad and its adjoining public plaza in Los Angeles.

title: A summer evening at the children’s park
paragraphs: I’ve added two recordings from the children’s area at Shenzhen Talent Park Phase II, filmed on a summer evening in 2025. Within this large urban park, the play area has a rich sequence of spaces and a scale that feels comfortable. It was a lovely evening, with the space full of laughter. A reminder of how much pleasure a good public space can bring to everyday life.
imageAlt: Illustration of the children’s play area at Shenzhen Talent Park Phase II.

title: Starting the Journal
paragraphs: I’m starting a Journal alongside the project archive. Collecting trips and new releases each have a bit of context that doesn’t always belong on a project page. I’ll use this space to share those updates and photographs from my visits.

title: A trip to Los Angeles
paragraphs: I was in Los Angeles as a presenter at this year’s ASLA conference and combined the trip with some recording for LENS. This time I visited Tongva Park in Santa Monica and The Broad in downtown Los Angeles, including the plaza beside the museum. Both will be joining the archive.
imageAlt: Curving paths, planted terraces and seating at Tongva Park in Santa Monica.

title: Smale Riverfront Park is online
paragraphs: Three recordings from my visit to Smale Riverfront Park are now on LENS: the swing pergola, a sculpture area and the water features. These are among the park’s more representative spaces, each with a distinct sense of scale.
imageAlt: Three views along the Ohio River

title: The first recordings on YouTube
paragraphs: The first LENS recordings are now on YouTube. I’ve started with Yongqing Fang and Huacheng Plaza in Guangzhou, with two viewpoints available for Huacheng Plaza. You can find the recordings and basic design information on their project pages.

title: LENS is online
paragraphs: LENS is now online at lens-vr.com. I’ve set it up as a home for the 360° recordings I’ve been collecting of contemporary urban public spaces. The collection is small for now, but I have more material from recent trips to add.

title: Summer fieldwork in China
paragraphs: I collected 360° recordings of several public-space projects during a summer visit to China. I’ll be adding these to LENS gradually as I prepare the individual project entries.

title: Choosing YouTube for the recordings
paragraphs: After weighing several hosting options, I’ve decided to use YouTube for the recordings in LENS. Device compatibility was the main consideration: the archive needs to be accessible on a range of VR headsets as well as ordinary computers, tablets and phones. YouTube seemed the best fit for making the same recordings available across these different devices.

title: A trip to Cincinnati
paragraphs: I combined the CELA conference in Cincinnati with visits to Smale Riverfront Park, Zaha Hadid’s Contemporary Arts Center and Fountain Square. I also went to the University of Cincinnati to see the campus landscapes by Hargreaves Associates. The photograph here is from the campus; I’ve included a few more from the rest of the trip below.
imageAlt: Lawns, terraced seating and paths on the University of Cincinnati campus.

title: A November visit to Seattle
paragraphs: I made a recording trip to Seattle in November, visiting several established landscape projects as well as the new Waterfront Park on Elliott Bay. The waterfront had celebrated its opening that September, shortly before my visit. I also had the chance to meet someone from GGN, who generously spent several hours chatting with me about design and the creative process at the practice. I really enjoyed the conversation!
